query: My employer, a state university, reserved 50% of teaching posts for certain castes and I was denied a job despite scoring higher. Is that constitutionally allowed, or does it violate my right to equality?
notes: Equality code: general guarantee (14) vs non-discrimination (15) vs public-employment equality + reservation carve-out (16(4)). Needs synthesis across all three; may need clarification on whether posts are 'backward class'.

query: Can the government ban a documentary critical of a sitting minister on the grounds that it threatens public order?
notes: Freedom of speech 19(1)(a) vs the reasonable-restriction grounds in 19(2). Single article, multi-clause; tests whether the model finds and weighs the restriction clause.

query: The police arrested my brother at midnight, didn't tell him why, and have held him for three days without seeing a magistrate. Which of his constitutional protections were breached?
notes: Life & liberty (21) + arrest/detention safeguards, 24-hour production, preventive-detention exceptions (22) + protections against self-incrimination/double-jeopardy (20). Clarify whether detention is preventive vs punitive.

query: If a fundamental right of mine is violated, should I approach the Supreme Court or the High Court, and is there any difference in what each can do?
notes: Constitutional remedies: SC writ jurisdiction (32, itself a fundamental right) vs wider HC writ jurisdiction (226) + laws inconsistent with FRs void (13). Comparative synthesis.

query: Can Parliament amend the Constitution to abolish judicial review entirely, or are there limits on the amendment power?
notes: Amendment power & procedure (368) vs void-if-inconsistent (13) vs guaranteed remedy (32). The 'basic structure' limit is doctrine (case law), not text — so text alone gives a PARTIAL answer; good for teaching honest 'the text says X, but courts have held Y' behaviour.

query: During a national emergency, can the government suspend my right to move the courts, and does that apply to every fundamental right?
notes: Proclamation of Emergency (352) + automatic suspension of Art 19 (358) + suspension of enforcement of rights (359) with the 20/21 carve-out. Multi-hop; clarify which emergency type.

query: On what grounds can the Union dismiss an elected state government and impose central rule, and how long can that last?
notes: President's Rule: failure of constitutional machinery (356) + Union's duty to protect states (355). Procedural: grounds, proclamation, duration limits, parliamentary approval.

query: Is India constitutionally required to have a Uniform Civil Code, and can I sue the government to enforce one?
notes: UCC directive (44) is a Directive Principle; DPSPs are non-justiciable (37). Correct answer is a REFUSAL of the 'sue to enforce' part — teaches the model to say what the tools/text cannot support.

query: What is the difference between the freedom to practise my religion and the freedom of a religious denomination to manage its own affairs, and can the state tax me to fund a particular religion?
notes: Individual religious freedom (25) vs denominational autonomy (26) vs no taxation for religion (27) vs religious instruction in state institutions (28). Four-article synthesis.

query: A state passed a law on a subject that a central law also covers, and the two conflict. Which law prevails, and does it matter whether the subject is in the state or concurrent list?
notes: Distribution of legislative powers (246) + extent of laws (245) + repugnancy between Union and State law (254). Needs the Seventh Schedule lists conceptually; clarify which list the subject sits in.
